spec: TRACK 8 — Elderly-vs-young-adult fall-kinematics validity (Action #23, docs/DATA_COLLECTION_PROTOCOL.md §2.2). SPARK's end-use population is elderly (per proposal scope, cited in Action #34's Velcro-closure rationale), but the human-subject collection protocol's inclusion criteria recruit healthy adults 18-35 (KEC student/faculty volunteers performing *simulated* falls). Research literature on how age affects fall kinematics (descent velocity, impact profile, pre-fall recovery attempts) and how comparable studies — including SisFall itself, which has both young and elderly subject groups — have handled or limited the young-adult-simulated-fall-as-elderly-proxy gap. Deliverable: a candid assessment of how much this limits SPARK's claims, and any protocol adjustments (e.g. slower/more deliberate fall execution instructions) that published studies use to partially compensate.
